newsitem.title: UK: Regent Pacific backs down on Hambros - paper.
newsitem.headline: Regent Pacific backs down on Hambros - paper.

text.p: Asian investment fund Regent Pacific Group has conceded defeat in its bid to get shareholder support for a plan to break up British investment bank Hambros Plc, the Evening Standard newspaper reported.

The Standard quoted Regent Pacific chairman Jim Mellon as saying shareholders had shown some sympathy for his plan but most had wanted to give the current Hambros management a chance to improve the bank's results.
A spokeswoman at Hambros declined to comment on the report.

Regent, which has a three percent stake in Hambro, argued that Hambros should return capital to shareholders by selling somes of its subsidiaries, particularly its 51 percent holding in estate agency Hambro Countrywide.
Asked by the Standard if he was conceding defeat, Mellon said: "To the extent thay have not followed our advice and are not showing evidence of returning money to shareholders, the answer is yes."
Earlier this week, Hambros chief Chips Keswick dismissed Regent's moves.
"Regent is a three percent shareholder and is perfectly entitled to (its) views. We are perfectly entitled not to share them," Keswick told Reuters in an interview.

The Hambro chief executive was speaking after the bank announced a return to profit in the first half of the year which, nevertheless, disappointed a market which had been expecting better results, especially from its "core" investment banking business.

Mellon told the Standard that Hambros share price should be around 390p to reflect the real net asset value of the company. Hambros shares were quoted 1/2p lower on Friday at 243-1/2p. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
